facts.text: Markkula et al., published in Accident Analysis & Prevention in 2016, found that brake responses in naturalistic rear-end emergencies depend on situational kinematics, such as gap-closing speed; this argues against using a single fixed reaction time.

facts.text: On-road evidence reported in a US DOT report and the McDonald et al. 2019 review found that evidence-accumulation models fitted to simulator data captured takeover braking better than fixed baseline reaction-time models.

facts.text: In an on-road virtual assessment of cyclist-overtaking Forward Collision Warning (FCW), estimated fatality reductions ranged from 53% to 96% depending on the driver response model; driver-model choice dominated the estimated benefit.
